sourceDiscovery.method: Real Chrome browser navigation (not blind HTTP) confirmed the entry page, category structure, category-level official counts, and per-product listing/detail markup independently for omegawatches.co.kr. Same 16 category slugs and same underlying Magento platform as the already-documented Omega Taiwan workflow were independently re-confirmed live, not assumed from the Taiwan example.
confirmedPublicEndpoints: https://www.omegawatches.co.kr/watches/{family}/{subcategory}/catalog?p={page}&ajax=1&noFilters=1 (JSON wrapper with html.products_list fragment, requires X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest header)
sourceDiscovery.rateLimitFinding: Repeated same-origin fetch() calls issued directly from page-context JavaScript (bypassing normal navigation) were silently rate-limited/hung by the site's bot defenses after roughly 10-12 requests in quick succession, regardless of added delays. Real top-level browser navigation (the `navigate` tool) was not observed to trigger this and remained reliable throughout. Collection was therefore restructured to use real per-page navigation for every page actually recorded as formal data: category pages via navigation to the plain (non-ajax) `?p=<lastPage>` URL, which this Magento theme's own client-side script hydrates cumulatively (rendering pages 1..N together) once given enough time to settle, confirmed by matching the official per-category count in a single navigation per category. Product detail pages (for dial/case technical data) were each visited individually via real navigation; the small number of fetch() calls used for the AJAX pagination check itself were paced at 1.5s+ and limited to short bursts after discovering the rate limit.

terminationEvidence: Every category's official count (as displayed on the entry page and re-confirmed on each category page's own 'Products list N' counter) was matched exactly by the unique product-card count collected for that category, using productUrl as the de-duplication key (an internal numeric source-product ID was not exposed in the listing markup on this site, unlike the Taiwan example; productUrl is a stable, reference-bearing substitute independently confirmed to be unique per configuration). No category showed unresolved further pagination beyond the point where accumulated unique cards matched the official count.
limitations: Dial color (rawDialText / data-code=watch_dial) was absent on the official product page for 34 of 554 references (6.1%), overwhelmingly concentrated in the 'Aqua Terra Shades' textile-strap/dial line (20 of 34) plus scattered gem-set or special-material Constellation/De Ville Prestige/Speedmaster 38 variants. These were independently spot-checked live (2 of the 34 are in the 19-item spot-check sample, both confirmed to genuinely lack the field on a fresh reload) and are recorded as dialDescription: null rather than guessed.

Omega Korea product pages do not state whether displayed KRW prices include VAT. Per this project's tax-research standard, priceType tax-include / taxRatePercent 10 was determined from a Korea National Tax Service written ruling (국세청 서면인터넷방문상담3팀-2350, 2007-08-22, citing 서면3팀-1695/2006-08-04 and 부가46015-1797/2000-07-26) establishing that when a price does not separately state VAT and it is unclear whether VAT is included, the amount is deemed VAT-inclusive at 10/110 of the stated price; this is a legal default/deeming rule, not an explicit statement by Omega itself, and is recorded here as such.

Nickname research (see nickname-research.json) found only candidates that were either already part of the watch's own official on-page name (e.g. '제임스 본드 탄생 60주년 기념' / James Bond 60th Anniversary is the literal official title of reference 210.55.42.20.99.001, not an unofficial nickname) or too loosely scoped across many references to satisfy this project's precise full-reference mapping requirement (e.g. generic press use of '본드 워치' for the Diver 300M line broadly). Result: PASS with 0 accepted results, not NOT RUN.

Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema validation was not run because no compatible validator (e.g. the `jsonschema` Python package) is installed in this environment; strict JSON parsing and manual field/type/pattern/uniqueness/cross-file checks equivalent to the schema's constraints were run instead and are recorded in validation-summary.json.
collectionAliases were left empty for all four collectionIds; no market-wide (not sub-collection-scoped) alias satisfied this project's precision bar during nickname research.
